About me

I am an engineer who is curious about how a whole system holds together: the sensor that measures something, the firmware that reads it, the backend that makes sense of it, and the screen where a person decides what to do next. I like building every one of those layers instead of a single piece in isolation, because the interesting failures happen at the seams between them. I am an electronics and communication engineer looking for electronics, embedded, IoT, hardware and research engineering roles where I can keep working across that whole stack and learn from people who build systems that last.

Automation Software Intern

ESAB India R&D · Internship

I owned the interface layer of a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) validation platform that replaces step-by-step manual testing of industrial welding equipment.

11tools delivered
3code repositories
18tickets closed, 3 epics
8hardware module replicas
WebHMI
Browser replicas of 8 hardware modules with component-level visualization, port-level monitoring, module configuration and live test execution. Telemetry streams at 5 updates per second, and every value on screen comes from the test backend, never from the page.
Test tooling
A test case designer with OCR and image-match checks and YAML export, plus an importer that turns a spreadsheet of about 1,160 rows across 22 sheets into runnable steps. Anything it cannot map safely stays a manual step. It never guesses.
Control panel
21 buttons and 4 encoders that drive real hardware, with an acknowledgement or error shown for every command. More than 20 review findings fixed along the way.
Architecture
Frontend, backend and test-simulation parts across a 6-layer stack, built as reusable module-specific workflows.
Presentation›Application›Domain›Service›HAL›Infrastructure
Process
Scrum/Agile with Jira alongside the ESAB Global R&D Automation Team, with features, workflows and architecture written up in low-level design documents.

The numbers count what I delivered, not time saved: I did not measure that, so I do not claim it. Code, screenshots, hardware specs and internal names stay private. certificate on LinkedIn
